historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes state-changing risk and user package need, but its example target and flash syntax are unsafe to execute generically.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds driver and firmware identity, compatibility, sequencing, reboot, array-health and recovery controls.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This case updates Windows RAID software and controller firmware; it must not be conflated with OS installation or read-only inventory.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Both artifacts and the exact controller must be cryptographically and physically identified before any state change.

original_test_intent: Update the approved Windows RAID driver and controller firmware, restart once, and verify the resulting versions exactly match the approved packages without storage, boot or event errors.
original_method: After critical approval, validate signed packages and stable controller identity, apply the vendor-supported driver/firmware sequence under continuous array and power monitoring, restart once through KVM/OOB and verify versions plus complete storage/event health.
manual_activity: User supplies and approves exact signed packages, target, sequence and recovery; operator supervises flash/restart via KVM/OOB; agent validates, executes only the approved command and captures evidence.
required_inputs: Controller model/serial/PCI identity and current driver/firmware
Signed driver and firmware packages, hashes, vendor tool/docs and target versions
Windows build plus compatibility and supported transition/rollback sequence
Healthy array, backup image, stable power, maintenance window and abort limits
safety_requirements: Bind the update to stable controller identity rather than /c0 numbering
Verify signatures, hashes, compatibility and sequence before execution
Require healthy non-rebuilding arrays, stable power and tested recovery
Preserve complete pre-update logs and stop on target/package ambiguity, updater/controller/array/power/boot/event error
Never force flash, erase, rebuild, auto-rollback or repeatedly restart
agent_execution_scope: Collect pre-update Windows driver, controller firmware, array and boot/health baseline
Validate packages and render the exact approved vendor command
Run only after command-level approval and capture full updater output/exit status
After one restart verify versions, arrays, mounts and logs; do not choose package/target or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target, artifacts, compatibility, sequence and rollback/recovery
Supervise the firmware boundary and own any controller/boot recovery
Review exact pre/post versions and health evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A vendor updater may be applicable, but assumed /c0 and a filename variable are not adequate identity or authorization; the example also omits the Windows driver and recovery sequence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the controller-specific vendor-documented Windows driver installer and firmware updater only after stable identity and signed-package validation, preserving full output and one approved restart.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Current-version check, driver and firmware updates, restart and source 5/10 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat driver replacement and firmware flash as a controlled two-artifact transaction with explicit before/after inventory and a single recovery-supervised restart.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds cryptographic provenance, exact target, compatibility, array-health and rollback evidence while preserving both updates.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No firmware or driver step is replaced by inventory-only checks.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Controller numbering may change across reboot and some firmware transitions are non-downgradable; stable hardware identity and vendor recovery limits govern.

project_override_considerations: If vendor documentation requires firmware before driver or an intermediate version, that approved path overrides generic ordering and must be recorded exactly.
expected_evidence: Approval, vendor documentation and compatibility/rollback matrix
Controller stable identity and pre-update driver/firmware/array state
Package hashes/signatures and exact updater commands/options
Full driver/firmware updater output, exit codes and timestamps
One-restart KVM/OOB record and exact post-update driver/provider/date plus controller firmware
Final array/drive/cache/boot/mount health, Windows events, BMC/SEL and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently requires both updates and restart verification; DeepSeek is incomplete but aligned on purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact packages, target and recovery are supplyable firmware-update prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Replaces a guessed controller flash example with signed-artifact, stable-target, sequenced driver/firmware update and recoverable post-restart validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A RAID driver and controller firmware jointly define the I/O path, and mismatched versions can fail only after restart. Controller indices are not stable identities and updater success does not prove array integrity, so acceptance requires signed artifacts, exact hardware binding, complete update output and post-boot version plus array/driver/event health.
